summary: Throttle ripple effect from health probes + warmups causing intermittent 429 waves
description: Issue summary: NimbusSearch reports recurring short 'waves' of 429 throttles affecting multiple routes and API keys within their dedicated pool. The pattern correlates with scheduled health probes and model warmup spikes from their ingestion fleet. Impact: Several customer-critical search ingestion jobs retry/fail, causing lag and backfill delays (customer reports ~20-30% of concurrent batches hitting 429 for 30-90s windows). Environment: prod/us-west (dedicated pool: dp-54321).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy 50 concurrent ingesters each running scheduled warmup + health probe (10s interval, no jitter) against /v1/embeddings endpoint.
2) Start a bulk import job that streams batches of 512 items per request (parallelism=40).
3) Observe 429s returned for a subset of requests; 429 bursts align with probe timestamps and warmup start times.
4) Re-run with probes disabled or with randomized jitter (0-30s) and observe 429s drop significantly.

comments: 2026-03-12T12:14:Support Agent (Priya): Thanks for the report — we're triaging. Can you confirm whether health probes and warmup flows use the same API key as ingestion?

2026-03-12T12:22:Customer (NimbusSearch - Elena): Yes, probes and workers share the same key for historical reasons. Probes hit /health and /v1/embeddings; warmups call a small prompt to load KV cache.

2026-03-12T13:00:SRE (Marco): Observed repeated short windows where tenant token accounting spikes. Probe-related requests are small but high-cardinality and coincide with token-bucket exhaustion across routes. Adding jitter reduced the observed 429s in a quick test.

2026-03-12T15:40:Support Agent (Priya): Temporary mitigation applied: advised customer to rotate probe traffic to a separate API key and introduced 0-20s jitter. Customer to report back on stability in the next 24h.
2026-03-13T09:05:Customer (Elena): After isolating probe key and adding jitter, 429 waves dropped from impacting 25% of batches to <2%. Still seeing occasional tail 429s during large scale warmups.
investigation_notes: Token-bucket telemetry shows tenant-level bucket refill is per-tenant per-window; many tiny high-frequency probes aggregate to sudden burst consumption that drains shared bucket.
Per-route accounting exists but is shadowed by tenant-level enforcement in dedicated pools when tenant bucket crosses zero — causes cross-route impact.
Probe requests are low-cost individually (token_cost ~16) but high QPS when synchronized; warmup operations cost larger tokens (256-512) and pushed the bucket negative while probes were running.
No evidence of serving-runtime kernel or GPU saturation — queue_depth increases but within autoscale thresholds. Root cause appears quota accounting and probe/warmup traffic patterns.
Relevant dashboards: /d/redwood/tenant-quota/dp-54321 and /d/redwood/route-throttle/nimbus; Slack thread #support-nimbussearch-54321 for raw traces.
Experiment: Introduced jitter on 10 ingesters and isolated probe key — immediate reduction in simultaneous token peaks.
resolution_notes: Workaround implemented: Customer created separate API key for health probes and configured probe jitter (0-20s). This reduced synchronized peaks and resolved the majority of 429 waves.

Short-term recommended configuration: - Use dedicated probe key with its own per-key quota or route that is exempted from tenant bulk-burst accounting. - Add random jitter to scheduled probes/warmups. - Stagger warmup start across ingesters.

Planned long-term actions: - Internal task (INT-4412) to implement probe/agent traffic classification so health-checks can be optionally excluded from tenant burst accounting in Dedicated mode. - Product doc update to recommend probe isolation and provide example k6/curl scripts (tracked in Confluence page).
Follow-up: Customer to monitor for 72 hours; if tail 429s persist we'll capture full token-bucket traces and consider temporary per-tenant burst-topup for migration window.
Status: Mitigation effective; ticket remains In Progress until long-term change or 72h stable window confirmed.
